**VERDICT: REJECT** **Overall Assessment**: The multi-step wizard implements several baseline ARIA attributes (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-live="polite"`), but exhibits severe architectural flaws in focus management, DOM hiding, and interactive state communication. Inactive step panels are hidden using CSS clipping and `aria-hidden="true"` while remaining fully focusable in the Tab sequence, creating ghost focus stops and critical keyboard accessibility failures. Furthermore, disabling the "Next" button on validation failure and unmounting the "Back" button on step reversion instantly dumps browser focus to `document.body`, disorienting screen reader and keyboard users. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions - **Prediction 1**: Inactive steps hidden with CSS clipping will retain focusable elements inside the DOM tab sequence without `display: none` or `inert`. *(Confirmed — CRITICAL)* - **Prediction 2**: Activating validation errors will trap or disorient focus when buttons disable dynamically. *(Confirmed — CRITICAL)* - **Prediction 3**: Focus will not advance to the new panel heading or first input upon navigating between wizard steps. *(Confirmed — MAJOR)* - **Prediction 4**: Error summary in `aria-live` will fail to provide actionable anchor links to target fields and will not announce error resolution. *(Confirmed — MAJOR)* - **Prediction 5**: Form inputs collecting personal identification data will lack standard `autocomplete` tokens. *(Confirmed — MAJOR)* --- ### Critical Findings (Blocks Access) #### 1. Focusable interactive inputs remain in the Tab order within `aria-hidden` step panels - **Evidence**: JSX lines 52–54, 67–69; CSS `.step-hidden` lines 43–49 ```jsx
``` ```css .step-hidden { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; } ``` - **Impacted Users**: Keyboard-only users, Screen reader users (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver). - **Why this matters**: `.step-hidden` visually clips the inactive panel into a 1px rectangle, and `aria-hidden="true"` removes it from the accessibility tree. However, the child `` elements (`#name`, `#email` on Step 1; `#street`, `#zip` on Step 0) remain natively focusable in the DOM. When a keyboard user tabs through the form, focus lands on invisible inputs inside the 1px rect. When a screen reader user lands on these fields, the browser enters an element marked `aria-hidden="true"` (violating the axe-core `aria-hidden-focus` rule), resulting in either total silence or unannounced inputs. - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), content hidden from users must not receive focus. - **Fix**: Replace `.step-hidden` and `aria-hidden` with `display: none` (e.g. `hidden` attribute) or apply the HTML `inert` attribute to inactive panels: ```jsx

Observe focus entering hidden inputs #street and #zip from Step 1. expected_behavior: Hidden step elements must be completely removed from the keyboard tab sequence. actual_behavior: Inactive panel inputs receive keyboard focus while clipped and aria-hidden. trend: new ``` --- #### 2. Disabling the "Next" button upon validation causes immediate focus loss to `document.body` - **Evidence**: JSX line 96: ```jsx ``` - **Impacted Users**: Keyboard-only users, Screen reader users. - **Why this matters**: When the user presses Enter or Space while focused on the "Next" button, `validate()` triggers. If errors exist, `hasErrors` becomes `true`, causing React to re-render the button with `disabled={true}`. In modern browser implementations, disabling an element that currently holds focus causes immediate blur, forcibly dropping focus to `document.body`. Focus is not routed to the error summary or the first invalid field. The user loses their context entirely and must re-tab through the entire page header and form. - **Expected Behavior**: Per WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and WCAG 3.2.1 (On Focus), focus must remain logical. When validation fails, focus should deliberately move to either the error summary container or the first invalid form control. - **Fix**: Never hard-disable the submission/navigation button when validation fails. Keep the button operable so keyboard users can re-trigger validation, or use `aria-disabled="true"` with pointer-events handling while managing focus directly: ```jsx // Inside validate(): if (Object.keys(errs).length > 0) { setErrors(errs); // Programmatically move focus to error container or first invalid input const firstInvalidId = Object.keys(errs)[0]; document.getElementById(firstInvalidId)?.focus(); return false; } ``` ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: focus-lost-on-disabled-next-button fingerprint: a92e441bc8f307d2 source: MultiStepForm.jsx:96 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order), WCAG 3.2.1 (On Focus) section_508_fpc_context: E205.4 / WCAG 2.0 A (2.4.3, 3.2.1) severity: CRITICAL perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, keyboard=HIGH, low_vision=LOW, cognitive=MEDIUM evidence: MultiStepForm.jsx:96: disabled={hasErrors} on active button element drops focus to document.body upon submission failure. reproduction_steps: 1. Tab to "Next" button on Step 0 with empty fields. 2. Press Enter. 3.
